title: Dynamic Off-Premise Pricing for Capacity-Constrained Dine-In Services
content: This paper studies when dynamic off-premise pricing creates economic value in a capacity-constrained dine-in service system. Customers choose among dine-in consumption, off-premise ordering, and no purchase, while the retailer adjusts the off-premise price according to current seat occupancy. We formulate the problem as a continuous-time Markov decision process and compare the optimal dynamic policy with the best constant off-premise price. We then use a global numerical analysis to examine how operating conditions, customer preferences, price sensitivity, and off-premise cost affect the profit gain from dynamic pricing. We conduct the analysis by solving the model, generating large simulation datasets using sampling methods, training a surrogate model, and using SHAP value to understand each parameter’s impact on the relative gain of dynamic pricing versus static pricing. The results show that dynamic pricing is not always more profitable than constant pricing. Its value is greatest when seating capacity is sufficiently scarce, dine-in demand is strong, customers can be redirected toward off-premise consumption, and off-premise pricing remains economically viable. Overall, dynamic off-premise pricing is most useful when congestion-management needs and customer diversion opportunities occur simultaneously.
